$comment: KluCode design tokens — the single source of truth. The website's tailwind.config.ts imports this file directly, so a change here reaches the site with no copy-paste step. Contrast ratios in `wcag` were computed against paper (#F2F4F1) and ink (#0C1A15); see 03-visual-identity.md for the rules they imply.

viridian.$comment: Generated by build_palette.py in OKLCH — do not hand-edit. Even perceptual lightness ladder, chroma peaking at 500/600 and tapering at both ends, and deliberate hue torsion (cooler tints, deeper shades). 500 is THE brand colour and is display-only: it fails AA for body text on both paper and ink.

stone.$comment: Generated by build_palette.py. Near-neutral by design: chroma 0.004-0.010, an order of magnitude below the old hand-picked scale, with the hue held steady instead of drifting 34 degrees. The neutrals must be somewhere the eye can rest, or the whole page reads as one muddy hue. 50 is paper, 950 is ink. 0 is pure white and carries no chroma at all: it is the raised-panel surface in light mode, and the only true neutral in the system.

semantic.$comment: Interface states only — form validation, status pills, alert boxes. These are NOT brand colours and never appear in marketing material or the logo. warningSurface is the one warm value left in the system, and it is confined to alert boxes on purpose: an alert that is not warm does not read as an alert.

dangerOnDark.$comment: danger is a single deep brick that was used as text-danger on form validation messages regardless of colour scheme. On the dark page it measures 2.00:1 and on a dark panel 1.59:1 — invisible, on the one string a user is required to be able to read. This is the same colour taken up the scale in OKLCH (L 0.441 -> 0.78, hue held at 28.8, chroma tapered 0.128 -> 0.10) so dark mode obeys the same raised-is-lighter rule as every other role: 7.95:1 on the page, 6.30:1 on a panel.

warm.$comment: Generated by build_palette.py. The system's ONE warm counterpoint, at hue 62 against viridian's 152. Two steps only, because it has exactly one job: the availability status dot, light and dark. 600 at L 0.620 is the lightest step that still clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 against the page (3.24:1) as a non-text indicator. Do not scatter this — a second warm accent and the counterpoint stops being one.

scene.$comment: Colours that exist only inside the WebGL crossroads on the homepage. Deliberately NOT emitted as CSS variables and deliberately not roles: nothing outside a 3D context may reach them, and a role nobody can reach is a role nobody can misuse. check_contrast.py audits roles, so it has nothing to say about these, which is correct: none of them is ever text on a surface.

glass.$comment: NAVIGATION LAYER ONLY. This used to dress ~27 elements per screen as 'clear glass'; measured, it was doing nothing. A 0.10 white fill with no border over a near-white page composited to 1.007:1 against that page — the cards had no edge at all in light mode — and both the 6px blur and the SVG displacement rim are no-ops over a smooth gradient, which is all that was ever behind them. Everything that carried content moved to the flat `.panel` material, which builds elevation out of surfaceRaised + border instead of faking it out of translucency. What survives is the sticky header capsule, the one element with real page content moving underneath it, which is also the only place Apple's own guidance puts this material. `fill` is deliberately high (0.86, was 0.10): the capsule passes over the ink footer as you scroll, and at a low fill the nav labels composite below AA against it. 0.86 is the measured floor — check_contrast.py composites every nav text role over the darkest and lightest backdrops the capsule can cross and fails the build below 4.5:1. lensBand/lensScale/fillStrong/edge/depth are gone with the lens and the variants that used them.

role.$comment: Two designed themes, not one theme and its inversion. Light builds hierarchy by going DARKER as elements recede; dark builds it by going LIGHTER as elements are raised, which is how physical light works and what dark mode actually needs. LIGHT MODE HAS A REAL ELEVATION STEP NOW, and this is the change the whole visual pass hinges on: surface and surfaceRaised used to BOTH be stone.50, a 1.0:1 step, i.e. no elevation existed at all. Dark mode had a genuine step (stone.900 over stone.950, 1.26:1) and that was the only reason dark mode looked better than light. The glass material was invented in this codebase to fake the elevation these tokens did not provide; with the page dropped to stone.100, panels raised to pure white (1.17:1) and the border moved to stone.300 (1.75:1 against a white panel), the elevation is real and the fake is unnecessary. surfaceAlt moves from viridian.50 to viridian.100 for the same reason: viridian.50 is LIGHTER than the new page, so tinted bands read as raised rather than recessed. viridian.100 sits at the page's own lightness and separates by chroma instead, which is a hue change rather than a competing elevation. Dark also uses off-white text rather than pure white, and moves the accent UP the scale where the chroma taper has already softened it — saturated colour on a dark ground vibrates. Dark muted text sits at stone.300, not 400: measured against the header capsule over a lit area, 400 came out at 4.31:1 — below AA. Dark grounds eat contrast that light grounds do not. The ink* roles are the closing slab at the foot of the page. They are deliberately NOT surfaceInverse: inverting the surface makes the footer follow the theme in the wrong direction, so dark mode ended up with a white footer glued to the bottom of a dark page. The footer is dark by design in both themes — in dark mode it lifts to stone.900 rather than inverting, which is the same raised-is-lighter rule the rest of dark mode follows.

display.$comment: Headlines and the wordmark. A sharp contemporary grotesque with genuine character — replaces Space Grotesk, which had become the default face of AI-generated sites.

body.$comment: Everything readable. Chosen for its German-language diacritics and long-text legibility.

mono.$comment: Eyebrow labels, tags, technical detail. The signal that says 'a developer built this'. Never body copy.

scale.$comment: Type scale, fluid between a 360px and a 1280px viewport.

space.$comment: 4px base grid. Section rhythm is deliberately generous — whitespace is the brand.

radius.$comment: Restrained. The logo's node circles supply the roundness; boxes stay close to square.

motion.$comment: Motion is functional, never decorative. Everything must be wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion.
